_schema.doc: Hand-curated census of the upstream public surface (ticket #15 on wayfinder map #14). Keyed by upstream export name; every name in parity/surface/upstream.json must appear exactly once, and no name may appear that is not in it — parity/census/build.mjs enforces both.

kind.enum-value: TS enum — a runtime object AND a type upstream
kind.callback: function type the library invokes on user-supplied handlers
kind.data: data shape crossing the library boundary
kind.options: config/options record consumed by a value export
kind.instance-api: method or bundle on ReactFlowInstance / viewport helpers
kind.internal-type: type with no consumer-facing runtime shadow

mechanism._doc: What could prove the *implementation*, not the JS-facing property. The distinction matters for `oracle`, which calls PureScript functions from PureScript, where currying and record returns are correct by construction — it can never prove anything about the shape a JavaScript caller receives. Values are unchanged from the L0/L1/L2 era; only the reading is pinned down.
mechanism.oracle: differential against the @psflow/oracle bundle — same input through PSFlow and vendored upstream JS
mechanism.dual-run-dom: mount both, drive both, diff DOM
mechanism.dual-run-props: mount a probe component in both, compare the props object it receives
mechanism.dual-run-hook: mount a probe component in both that calls the hook, compare the returned value
mechanism.dual-run-callback: drive both, record callback invocations and payloads, compare
mechanism.dual-run-api: call the same imperative method on both instances, compare return and effect
mechanism.dual-run-value: import the symbol from both and compare the runtime value directly
mechanism.none: no runtime existence on either side — surface-parity name presence is the whole story

gates._doc: A browser gate is written `<suite>:<spec file>` when a spec asserts the export directly and `<suite>-indirect:<spec file>` when the spec only mounts or traverses it. The spec is named because the manifest can only say an export has *crossed*; gated on a surface additionally needs some spec that entered through that door to assert on it. build.mjs fails if a named spec file does not exist, and reads each spec to decide which surface it entered through — so an export's surface columns follow its specs when a spec migrates.
gates.surface: implicit for every row and never written here — npm run parity:surface, name presence only
gates.surface-behavior: implicit for the enum and pure-function exports listed by parity/surface/behavior.mjs. JS surface: the gate imports and compares both barrels.
gates.boundary: npm run parity:boundary mount checks. JS surface: it imports index.js; written on each export whose crossing it directly checks.
gates.surface-props: npm run parity:surface prop-member diff (name-only, no member types). PureScript surface: it reads the records in src/React/Types/*.purs.
gates.function: spago test differential against the @psflow/oracle bundle. PureScript surface: it imports System.Utils.* directly.
gates.conformance:<spec>: npm run test:conformance — that spec asserts this directly
gates.conformance-indirect:<spec>: npm run test:conformance — mounted or traversed by that spec, but nothing specific to it is asserted
gates.smoke:<spec>: npm run test:smoke — that spec asserts this directly. No row carries one since issue 61: the smoke suite is liveness only, and its eight hand-authored parity assertions retired into the net per test, recorded in parity/system/corpus/retirement-debt.mjs.
gates.smoke-indirect:<spec>: npm run test:smoke — mounted or traversed, nothing specific asserted
gates._retired: A node-props:<spec> pair stood beside these for the PSFlow-specific NodeProps guard. It retired into the net (issue 61) through the dom section rather than the props one its condition named — parity/system/corpus/retirement-debt.mjs says why — and its spec is gone; what the net drives is parity/system/coverage.md, never a column here.

Background: No assertion targets it on either browser suite: the smoke suite mounts a default Background and the ColorMode driver mounts one too, neither saying anything about it. Its JS-shaped props and no-props mount are gated on the JS surface by parity:boundary. What drives its variant, gap, size and offset is the net — see parity/system/coverage.md.
BaseEdge: path, interactionWidth and markers asserted by generic-edges.
BezierEdge: getBezierPath has function parity; the component is only rendered as the fixture's default edge type.
ControlButton: Rendered inside Controls; the exported component with custom children is never mounted.
Controls: Mounted by the smoke suite's liveness page and by the ColorMode driver, with no assertion on either. Its JS-shaped props and no-props mount are gated on the JS surface by parity:boundary. The zoom-in-moves-the-transform assertion retired into the net (issue 61) — `controls-default-zoom` presses all three buttons where the assertion pressed one.
EdgeText: Mounted for the fixture's string labels. The interactionWidth case depends on its measured background for the click target, but no assertion is specifically about label rendering.
EdgeToolbar: getEdgeToolbarTransform has function parity; the component is never mounted.
Handle: connect and connectable=false asserted by generic-nodes. The connectingfrom class assertion retired into the net (issue 61), which compares the class mid-gesture and after the drop as two scenarios. Upstream's two defaults and the enum conversion are gated on the JS surface by parity:boundary, mounted inside a node component rather than in the flow. ToolbarNode.tsx mounts a target and a source handle, which is the only place a consumer's own component mounts one, but asserts nothing about either.
MiniMap: Mounted by the smoke suite's liveness page and by the ColorMode driver, with no assertion on either. Its JS-shaped props and no-props mount are gated on the JS surface by parity:boundary. The renders-and-is-clickable assertion retired into the net (issue 61); node rendering, the mask and pan/zoom are the net's too.
MiniMapNode: Surfaced by ticket 058 — `miniMapNode` on the PureScript surface, and passthrough on the JS surface, so a JS consumer importing it now gets a value rather than undefined. Its shape already agrees with upstream (memoized, arity 1); boundary stage 4 crosses its props.
NodeResizeControl: parity:boundary mounts it with no props inside a node component and holds its three enum converters; nothing drives a resize, so its handlers are reachable and undriven. Known-wrong — ticket 073 (XYResizer drag lifecycle).
NodeResizer: parity:boundary mounts it with no props inside a node component. Its four handlers cross but nothing drives a resize. Known-wrong — ticket 073.
NodeToolbar: getNodeToolbarTransform has function parity; positioning and default behaviour asserted by generic-node-toolbar. parity:boundary holds the pattern-match case and that its converters run, mounted inside a node component; it cannot assert the DOM, because the toolbar portals into a flow root a server render does not have.
Panel: Its required position, enum conversion and children pass-through are gated on the JS surface by parity:boundary. The ColorMode fixture also mounts it, but asserts only the wrapper's colorMode class.
ReactFlow: More gates touch this than any other export — the nodes, edges, pane and props specs all drive it, and the smoke suite's liveness tests mount it without asserting anything about it.
ReactFlowProvider: The retired PureScript smoke page mounted it, but no JS-surface driver does yet.
SimpleBezierEdge: getSimpleBezierPath has function parity; component never mounted.
SmoothStepEdge: getSmoothStepPath has function parity; component never mounted.
StepEdge: Upstream StepEdge is SmoothStepEdge at borderRadius 0, which function parity's generated domain covers; component never mounted.
StraightEdge: getStraightPath has function parity; component never mounted.
BackgroundVariant: Upstream runtime enum object, from @xyflow/react rather than @xyflow/system. Crossed by the boundary module (stage 1); surface parity deep-compares the frozen JS-surface object against upstream.
ConnectionLineType: Surface parity deep-compares the frozen JS-surface object against upstream, including Bezier's non-obvious string value "default" rather than "bezier".
ConnectionMode: Crossed by the boundary module (stage 1); surface parity deep-compares the frozen JS-surface object against upstream.
MarkerType: Surface parity deep-compares the frozen JS-surface object. Upstream's unchanged edges fixture also imports Arrow and ArrowClosed and asserts the marker URLs those values produce.
PanOnScrollMode: Crossed by the boundary module (stage 1); surface parity deep-compares the frozen JS-surface object against upstream.
Position: Crossed by the boundary module (stage 1); surface parity deep-compares the frozen JS-surface object against upstream.
ResizeControlVariant: Crossed by the boundary module (stage 1); surface parity deep-compares the frozen JS-surface object against upstream.
SelectionMode: Crossed by the boundary module (stage 1); surface parity deep-compares the frozen JS-surface object against upstream.
getNodesBounds: Oracled by ticket 039. Bounded claim: the arithmetic from positions and dimensions to a rect, with no nodeLookup on either side. The measured DOM dimensions that feed it stay out of reach of any oracle, so this does not close the Measurement and rounding question.
getViewportForBounds: Oracled by ticket 030: the fitView zoom formula agrees with upstream, so the spike's 1.03145-vs-1.05466 gap came from the inputs, not the arithmetic. Also traversed by fitView in the smoke fixtures, where nothing about its result is asserted.
addEdge: Function parity compares results and refusals; generic-nodes proves the JS calling convention by connecting nodes through the driver and asserting the added edge.
applyEdgeChanges: Function parity compares semantics; generic-edges proves the JS calling convention by selecting and deleting controlled edges through the driver.
applyNodeChanges: Function parity compares semantics; generic-nodes proves the JS calling convention by selecting, moving and deleting controlled nodes through the driver.
reconnectEdge: Oracled by ticket 039, on both channels, across both shouldReplaceId settings.
isEdge: Oracled by ticket 039 over all 16 key combinations — the guard's whole input domain, exhausted rather than sampled. Objects only: upstream's `in` test throws on a primitive where PSFlow answers false.
isNode: Oracled by ticket 039 over all 16 key combinations — the guard's whole input domain, exhausted rather than sampled. Objects only: upstream's `in` test throws on a primitive where PSFlow answers false.
experimental_useOnEdgesChangeMiddleware: parity:boundary gates that it accepts a JS-shaped middleware function; acceptance is the ceiling, as for the flow-level callbacks.
experimental_useOnNodesChangeMiddleware: parity:boundary gates that it accepts a JS-shaped middleware function; acceptance is the ceiling, as for the flow-level callbacks.
useConnection: parity:boundary gates that the connection state it returns is the JS-shaped one `onConnectEnd` receives, not the PureScript sum type.
useEdges: parity:boundary gates the array it returns and that its edges are JS-shaped.
useEdgesState: parity:boundary gates the JS-surface three-slot array, JS-shaped values, and both setter forms. The ColorMode driver also traverses it without a hook-specific assertion.
useHandleConnections: parity:boundary gates that its parameter takes upstream's `type` rather than ps-flow's `handleType`.
useInternalNode: parity:boundary gates that a node that is not there answers `undefined` rather than a PureScript `Maybe`.
useKeyPress: parity:boundary gates both call forms — bare, and with a key code and options. Four test-debt rows (077: #5090, #5118, #5263, #4880) land on this hook's focus handling.
useNodeConnections: parity:boundary gates the `id` rename its parameter carries, and that calling it outside a node reports so as upstream does. One test-debt row (077: #4949).
useNodeId: parity:boundary gates that it answers `null` outside a node — the one place on this surface where `null` and `undefined` mean different things.
useNodes: parity:boundary gates the array it returns and that its nodes are JS-shaped.
useNodesData: parity:boundary gates the overload upstream declares and ps-flow's single signature does not: one id answers one `{ id, type, data }` pick or `null`, an array answers an array.
useNodesInitialized: parity:boundary gates both call forms — with its options bag and without, which upstream allows by defaulting the parameter.
useNodesState: parity:boundary gates the JS-surface three-slot array, JS-shaped values, and both setter forms. The ColorMode driver also traverses it without a hook-specific assertion. One test-debt row (078: #5120, fitView for uncontrolled flows).
useOnSelectionChange: parity:boundary gates that it accepts a JS-shaped handler; acceptance is the ceiling, as for the flow-level callbacks.
useOnViewportChange: parity:boundary gates that it accepts JS-shaped handlers. A server render runs no effects, so acceptance is the ceiling here and the installation is the net's.
useReactFlow: parity:boundary gates the JS-surface instance this returns: all 32 members present, each taking its arguments in one call, the readers answering values rather than unrun `Effect` thunks, and the eleven asynchronous methods answering real promises. The whole imperative API hangs off this hook; four test-debt rows (078: #5276, #5723, #5722, #5012) land on it.
useStore: Crossed in shape only: callable at upstream's arity, and refusing at the call. What it would hand over is the internal store state, an 85-field PureScript record with no JS shape. parity:boundary gates the refusal, the same way it gates the deferred props'.
useStoreApi: Crossed in shape only, and refusing at the call, for the same reason as `useStore`. parity:boundary gates the refusal.
useUpdateNodeInternals: parity:boundary gates that it returns a callable one-argument updater, and that the updater takes upstream's `string | string[]` in both forms.
useViewport: parity:boundary gates that it returns `{ x, y, zoom }` rather than an unrun thunk.
Align: getNodeToolbarTransform takes align; toolbar positioning asserted.
BackgroundProps: Background is mounted with every prop unset on both surfaces; no prop is asserted.
BaseEdgeProps: interactionWidth and path exercised via the fixture edges.
BezierPathOptions: curvature swept by the getBezierPath property.
BuiltInEdge: Type-only both sides. Upstream unions the built-in variants by discriminating on a string-literal `type`; PS `Edge e` carries `type :: Maybe String`, so there are no distinct types to union. Documented divergence — allowlisted, and src/React.purs's header.
BuiltInNode: Type-only both sides. As `BuiltInEdge`: PS `Node n` carries `type :: Maybe String`. Documented divergence — allowlisted, and src/React.purs's header.
ColorMode: generic-props asserts the light and dark wrapper classes.
Connection: generic-nodes asserts an edge appears after connecting; the onConnect payload shape is never inspected by a browser suite. The net's callbacks section compares it — see parity/system/coverage.md.
ConnectionLineComponent: Surfaced on the PureScript surface by ticket 058. PS types it `ConnectionLineComponentProps n -> JSX` — the shape `ReactFlowProps.connectionLineComponent` has always held — rather than upstream's `ComponentType<Props>`.
ConnectionLineComponentProps: The connection line is never rendered by any fixture.
ControlProps: PSFlow renames it ControlsProps; cancelled on both sides by the allowlist. Type-only, so the rename cannot reach a JS consumer.
Edge: Selection, class, style, hidden, animated, zIndex, aria-label and deletion all asserted by generic-edges.
EdgeAddChange: Constructor of the PS EdgeChange sum type. No browser gate inspects change shapes; the net's callbacks section does — see parity/system/coverage.md.
EdgeChange: Selection and removal changes pass from the controlled flow through the JS driver and applyEdgeChanges; the spec proves the fields those operations need, not the complete payload.
EdgeComponentWithPathOptions: Surfaced on the PureScript surface by ticket 058, and load-bearing: `BezierEdgeProps`, `SmoothStepEdgeProps` and `StepEdgeProps` are now defined through it instead of restating the nineteen shared members each.
EdgeLabelOptions: String labels and the default measured background are reached by generic-edges; custom label styles, padding, visibility and border radius are still undriven.
EdgeMarker: getMarkerId has function parity; marker-start/marker-end URLs asserted by generic-edges.
EdgeProps: Prop-member names gated on the PureScript surface by the surface-parity prop diff (ticket 071 renamed edgeType to type). No component reads the props object at runtime — unlike the NodeProps guard.
EdgeRemoveChange: Constructor of the PS EdgeChange sum type.
EdgeReplaceChange: Constructor of the PS EdgeChange sum type.
EdgeSelectionChange: Constructor of the PS EdgeChange sum type.
EdgeTypes: PSFlow renames it EdgeTypesMap; type-only, so the rename cannot reach a JS consumer.
EdgeWrapperProps: Internal wrapper; observable only as the DOM it produces.
FitView: fitView runs when the smoke suite's liveness session presses the fit-view control, but no assertion targets the resulting viewport. The spike's fitView zoom divergence lives here.
FitViewParams: Surfaced on the PureScript surface by ticket 058 (`System.Utils.Graph`).
GeneralHelpers: Surfaced on the PureScript surface by ticket 058. `ReactFlowInstance` is now assembled from `GeneralHelpersRow` extended by `ViewportHelperFunctionsRow`, which is upstream's `&` written the PS way, instead of transcribing both halves into one record.
GetBezierPathParams: Surfaced on the PureScript surface by ticket 058, as a TS-name alias of PS `BezierPathParams`; both names resolve.
GetMiniMapNodeAttribute: Surfaced on the PureScript surface by ticket 058; the minimap's three node-attribute accessors on `MiniMapProps` and `MiniMapNodesProps` are typed through it.
GetSmoothStepPathParams: Surfaced on the PureScript surface by ticket 058, as a TS-name alias of PS `SmoothStepPathParams`.
GetStraightPathParams: Surfaced on the PureScript surface by ticket 058, as a TS-name alias of PS `StraightPathParams`.
HandleProps: connectable=false and handle position attributes asserted by generic-nodes. The smoke suite's liveness page mounts handles on both of its nodes and asserts nothing. ToolbarNode.tsx sets type and position on both of its handles and asserts neither.
HandleType: Surfaces as data-handlepos / handle classes, which the connect specs locate on. ToolbarNode.tsx passes both members and asserts neither; the smoke suite's liveness page renders both and asserts neither.
KeyCode: Delete-key presses drive the deletion specs, but only the default key codes.
MiniMapNodeProps: Surfaced on the PureScript surface by ticket 058 (`React.Types.Component`).
MiniMapNodes: Upstream names this props record after the component that takes it. Surfaced on the PureScript surface by ticket 058, as a TS-name alias of PS `MiniMapNodesProps`; both names resolve.
MiniMapProps: MiniMap is mounted with every prop unset on both surfaces; no prop is asserted.
NoConnection: Nullary constructor of the PS ConnectionState, not a standalone type (allowlisted, ticket 054).
Node: Selection, drag, delete, hidden, class, style all asserted by generic-nodes.
NodeAddChange: Constructor of the PS NodeChange sum type.
NodeChange: Selection, position and removal changes pass through the JS driver and applyNodeChanges; the spec proves the fields those operations need, not the complete payload.
NodeDimensionChange: Constructor of the PS NodeChange sum type.
NodeHandle: Surfaced on the PureScript surface by ticket 058 (`System.Types.Node`).
NodePositionChange: Constructor of the PS NodeChange sum type; the change fired by every node drag, and its shape is ungated.
NodeProps: Prop-member names gated on the PureScript surface by the surface-parity prop diff. Its runtime guard — node-props.spec.ts, which asserted eight hand-written strings against a PSFlow-only page — retired on the net (issue 61): `nodes/props-record.ts` renders the record into the DOM on both sides and `node-props-record-parented` drives it. Ticket 069 closed the xPos/yPos rename here after it survived from 12.3.5 as a printed-not-failed diff.
NodeRemoveChange: Constructor of the PS NodeChange sum type.
NodeReplaceChange: Constructor of the PS NodeChange sum type.
NodeResizerProps: NodeResizer is never mounted and is known-wrong (073).
NodeSelectionChange: Constructor of the PS NodeChange sum type.
NodeToolbarProps: position, align and offset all driven by generic-node-toolbar.
NodeTypes: PSFlow renames it NodeTypesMap. generic-nodes mounts a custom nodeTypes map for its drag-handle node; the custom-default fallback is known-wrong (ticket 075).
NodeWrapperProps: Internal wrapper; observable as the .react-flow__node DOM the node specs assert on.
OnConnect: generic-nodes observes only that an edge appeared after connecting nodes and never inspects the callback payload. The smoke suite's click-connect assertion retired into the net (issue 61).
OnEdgesChange: Selecting and deleting controlled edges can update the asserted DOM only through the driver's onEdgesChange callback.
OnError: One test-debt row (076: #5052, error when dragging an uninitialized node).
OnMoveEnd: One test-debt row (078: #5547, always call onMoveEnd when onMoveStart was called).
OnNodeDrag: One test-debt row (076: #5450, call onNodeDrag while autopan is ongoing).
OnNodesChange: generic-nodes observes controlled node selection, movement and deletion through the JS-surface driver, without inspecting the complete payload. The repo's only callback assertion — the smoke suite's onNodesChange-fires-on-drag — retired into the net (issue 61), where the callbacks section compares the exact sequence with its arguments; that it was the only one is why the retirement is recorded per test.
PanelPosition: The ColorMode driver mounts a top-right panel; position is not asserted. Two test-debt rows (079: #5252, #5362).
ReactFlowActions: PS models the action half of the store as constructors of `React.Store.Action.Action`, a sum type a pure reducer folds, so there is no record for this name to denote. Documented divergence — allowlisted, and src/React.purs's header.
ReactFlowInstance: The entire imperative API — zoomIn/zoomOut/setViewport/screenToFlowPosition/toObject/updateNode/deleteElements — is reachable by no gate. Six test-debt rows land here.
ReactFlowProps: Prop-member names gated on the PureScript surface by the surface-parity prop diff; a minority of members (selectable/draggable/deletable/connectable/minZoom/maxZoom/panOnScroll/defaultViewport/autoPan*/colorMode/nodeTypes) are driven by the conformance specs. The gate is name-only — a member whose type changed upstream still passes.
ReactFlowState: Observable through useStore selectors; no gate uses one.
ReactFlowStore: Surfaced on the PureScript surface by ticket 058, as a TS-name alias of `ReactFlowState`, which mirrors upstream's `ReactFlowStore` field by field.
Rect: Shape marshalled by the geometry properties.
ResizeControlLineProps: Props of upstream's internal `ResizeControlLine`. PS has no such component — `nodeResizeControl` serves both variants off one props record, selected by `variant` — so there is nothing for a second record to describe. Documented divergence — allowlisted, and src/React.purs's header.
ResizeControlProps: Surfaced on the PureScript surface by ticket 058, as a TS-name alias of PS `NodeResizeControlProps`; both names resolve.
SelectionRect: Shift-drag multi-select is asserted by its effect (nodes selected), not by the rect.
SmoothStepPathOptions: borderRadius, offset and stepPosition swept by the getSmoothStepPath property.
SnapGrid: Marshalled by the snapPosition and pointToRendererPoint properties.
Transform: Marshalled by pointToRendererPoint/rendererPointToPoint; the viewport transform string is read by the pane specs.
UseNodeConnectionsParams: Surfaced on the PureScript surface by ticket 058 (`React.Hook.NodeConnections`).
Viewport: Pan, wheel-zoom, minZoom, maxZoom and initial viewport asserted by the pane specs, via the transform string.
ViewportHelperFunctionOptions: Carries the ease/interpolate members from upstream #5276 — the test-debt row ticket 078 flags as most worth attention.
ZIndexMode: Four z-index assertions in generic-edges, including the two sub-flow cases.
